title: Toasted Oat and Sage Country Gravy
description: Toasted oats and rubbed sage give this milk gravy a nutty flavor that works with turkey, chicken or soft grits.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

steps.title: Toast the oats
steps.text: Stir {oats} in the dry HexClad over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes until lightly fragrant.

steps.title: Cook until soft
steps.text: Add {broth} and {milk}. Bring to a bare simmer and stir for 6–8 minutes until the oat flakes are fully tender.

steps.title: Blend the oat milk
steps.text: Puree the warm oat mixture until silky in a deep heatproof jug.

steps.title: Toast the sage roux
steps.text: Melt {butter} in the emptied skillet. Whisk in {flour}, {sage} and {pepper} and cook over medium-low for 1–2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish the country gravy
steps.text: Slowly whisk the oat mixture into the roux. Simmer gently for 2–3 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 1/2 cups total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle over braised poultry. For breakfast, stir the gravy into hot grits until both flow from the spoon.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: Toast the oats a day ahead or refrigerate the blended oat base until dinner. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze for up to 1 month. The oats thicken on standing, so whisk in a little water when reheating. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion over medium-low heat, whisking to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Whisk off heat until smooth. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. For dairy-free country gravy, use plain unsweetened oat milk and avocado oil in the same quantities as the milk and butter. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 36 kcal, 2.0 g protein, 4.0 g total carbohydrate, 1.4 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 22 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal.
